questions.q:
With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:
1. A private member's bill is a bill presented by a Member of Parliament who is not elected but only nominated by the President of India.
2. Recently, a private member's bill has been passed in the Parliament of India for the first time in its history.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A private member's bill is any bill moved by an MP who is not a minister, whether elected or nominated. Fourteen private members' bills have become law since 1952, so neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
With reference to the difference between the culture of Rigvedic Aryans and Indus Valley people, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Rigvedic Aryans used the coat of mail and helmet in warfare whereas the people of Indus Valley Civilization did not leave any evidence of using them.
2. Rigvedic Aryans knew gold, silver and copper whereas Indus Valley people knew only copper and iron.
3. Rigvedic Aryans had domesticated the horse whereas there is no evidence of Indus Valley people having been aware of this animal.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Harappans used gold, silver, copper and lead, but not iron, which came around 1000 BCE; so 2 is wrong. Rigvedic texts mention armour and helmets, and the horse was central to Aryan life with little Harappan evidence of it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q: 'Recognition of Prior Learning Scheme' is sometimes mentioned in the news with reference to
o: Certifying the skills acquired by construction workers through traditional channels.
Enrolling the persons in Universities for distance learning programmes.
Reserving some skilled jobs to rural and urban poor in some public sector undertakings.
Certifying the skills acquired by trainees under the National Skill Development Programme.
questions.e: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills people learnt informally, without a formal course. Its first pilot was for construction workers, before it became part of PMKVY.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q: From the ecological point of view, which one of the following assumes importance in being a good link between the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats?
questions.e: Sathyamangalam in western Tamil Nadu lies where the Western and Eastern Ghats meet, forming a wildlife corridor between them.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q: One of the implications of equality in society is the absence of
questions.e: Equality means that opportunities and treatment are not fixed by birth or status, so it requires ending special privileges for a few.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of Trade Related Analysis of Fauna and Flora in Commerce (TRAFFIC):
1. TRAFFIC is a bureau under United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
2. The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: TRAFFIC is a wildlife trade monitoring network set up by WWF and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau. Its mission is to ensure trade in wild plants and animals does not threaten nature.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q: Which principle among the following was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution?
o: Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Participation of workers in the management of industries
Right to work, education and public assistance
Securing living wage and human conditions of work to workers
questions.e: Article 43A, on workers' participation in the management of industries, was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). The other three were in the original Constitution.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rights are claims of the State against the citizens.
Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the Constitution of a State.
Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.
Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many.
questions.e: A right is a justified claim of the individual that the State must respect and protect, so rights are claims of citizens against the State.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q: Which of the following gives 'Global Gender Gap Index' ranking to the countries of the world?
questions.e: The Global Gender Gap Index is published annually by the World Economic Forum.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Smart India Hackathon 2017?
1. It is a centrally sponsored scheme for developing every city of our country into Smart Cities in a decade.
2. It is an initiative to identify new digital technology innovations for solving the many problems faced by our country.
3. It is a programme aimed at making all the financial transactions in our country completely digital in a decade.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Smart India Hackathon is a nationwide competition where students build digital solutions to real problems posed by ministries. It is not a smart cities or digital payments scheme.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?
1. It decides the RBI's benchmark interest rates.
2. It is a 12-member body including the Governor of RBI and is reconstituted every year.
3. It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The MPC fixes the policy repo rate. It has six members, is chaired by the RBI Governor, and external members serve four years, so 2 and 3 are wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements:
1. It is a song and dance performance.
2. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance.
3. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds of Lord Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Sankirtana of Manipur combines singing, drumming and dancing to narrate the life of Krishna. Drums (pung) and cymbals are both used, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q:
Who among the following was/were associated with the introduction of Ryotwari Settlement in India during the British rule?
1. Lord Cornwallis
2. Alexander Read
3. Thomas Munro
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Ryotwari settlement was first tried by Alexander Read and developed by Thomas Munro. Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q:
In the context of solving pollution problems, what is/are the advantage/advantages of bioremediation technique?
1. It is a technique for cleaning up pollution by enhancing the same biodegradation process that occurs in nature.
2. Any contaminant with heavy metals such as cadmium and lead can be readily and completely treated by bioremediation using microorganisms.
3. Genetic engineering can be used to create microorganisms specifically designed for bioremediation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Bioremediation speeds up natural biodegradation and can use genetically engineered microbes. Heavy metals like cadmium and lead cannot be broken down by microbes, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q14
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q: The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 provided for
o: the participation of workers in the management of industries.
arbitrary powers to the management to quell industrial disputes.
an intervention by the British Court in the event of a trade dispute.
a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes.
questions.e: The Trade Disputes Act 1929 set up Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation and restricted strikes in public utility services.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in
questions.e: Local self-government transfers power to elected local bodies so people decide local matters: this is democratic decentralisation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principles of State Policy constitute limitations upon
1. legislative function.
2. executive function.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines (Article 37), so they are not legal limits on the legislature or executive. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q17

questions.q: The term ‘Digital Single Market Strategy’ seen in the news refers to
questions.e: The Digital Single Market Strategy (2015) is a European Commission plan to merge the EU's national digital markets into one.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q: At one of the places in India, if you stand on the seashore and watch the sea, you will find that the sea water recedes from the shore line a few kilometres and comes back to the shore, twice a day, and you can actually walk on the sea floor when the water recedes. This unique phenomenon is seen at
questions.e: At Chandipur in Odisha the gently sloping shore lets the sea recede up to 5 km at low tide, so people can walk on the sea bed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (PBPT Act)’, consider the following statements:
1. A property transaction is not treated as a benami transaction if the owner of the property is not aware of the transaction.
2. Properties held benami are liable for confiscation by the Government.
3. The Act provides for three authorities for investigations but does not provide for any appellate mechanism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The amended Benami Act treats a deal as benami even if the owner is unaware, allows confiscation of benami property, and provides an Appellate Tribunal. Only 2 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q:
Due to some reasons, if there is a huge fall in the population of species of butterflies, what could be its likely consequence/consequences?
1. Pollination of some plants could be adversely affected.
2. There could be a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants.
3. It could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders and birds.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Butterflies are pollinators and food for wasps, spiders and birds, so their decline hurts both. They play no role in controlling fungal diseases of crops.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q:
It is possible to produce algae based biofuels, but what is/are the likely limitation(s) of developing countries in promoting this industry?
1. Production of algae based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents.
2. Setting up and engineering the algae based biofuel production requires high level of expertise/technology until the construction is completed.
3. Economically viable production necessitates the setting up of large scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Algae can be grown on land in ponds or photobioreactors, so 1 is false. The real hurdles are high technical expertise and the large scale needed, which raises ecological and social concerns.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q22

questions.q:
Which of the following are the objectives of ‘National Nutrition Mission’?
1. To create awareness relating to malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers.
2. To reduce the incidence of anaemia among young children, adolescent girls and women.
3. To promote the consumption of millets, coarse cereals and unpolished rice.
4. To promote the consumption of poultry eggs.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan) creates awareness about malnutrition among mothers and aims to reduce anaemia and stunting. Promoting millets or eggs is not among its objectives.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Factories Act, 1881 was passed with a view to fix the wages of industrial workers and to allow the workers to form trade unions.
2. N.M. Lokhande was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in British India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: The Factories Act 1881 dealt mainly with child labour and working conditions, not wages or unions. N.M. Lokhande, who founded the Bombay Mill Hands Association (1884), pioneered labour organising.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
In the context of mitigating the impending global warming due to anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide, which of the following can be the potential sites for carbon sequestration?
1. Abandoned and uneconomic coal seams
2. Depleted oil and gas reservoirs
3. Subterranean deep saline formations
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Captured CO₂ can be stored in unmineable coal seams, depleted oil and gas reservoirs and deep saline formations. All three are standard storage sites.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q: The object of the Butler Committee of 1927 was to
o: Define the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments.
Define the powers of the Secretary of State for India.
Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.
questions.e: The Butler Committee (1927) examined relations between the Paramount Power and the princely states.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q: The term ‘Domestic Content Requirement’ is sometimes seen in the news with reference to
o: Developing solar power production in our country
Granting licences to foreign T.V. channels in our country
Exporting our food products to other countries
Permitting foreign educational institutions to set up their campuses in our country
questions.e: Domestic Content Requirements under India's National Solar Mission required Indian-made solar cells and modules; the US challenged them at the WTO.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Nuclear Security Summits are periodically held under the aegis of the United Nations.
2. The International Panel on Fissile Materials is an organ of International Atomic Energy Agency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Nuclear Security Summits (2010-16) were a US-led process, not a UN one. The International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent expert group, not part of the IAEA.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q: Who among the following can join the National Pension System (NPS)?
o: Persons of age from 21 to 55 only
All State Government employees joining the services after the date of notification by the respective State Governments
All Central Government employees including those of Armed Forces joining the services on or after 1st April, 2004
questions.e: NPS applies to State Government employees joining after their State notifies it. NRIs can join, the age band was not 21-55, and the armed forces are excluded.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q:
With reference to river Teesta, consider the following statements:
1. The source of river Teesta is the same as that of Brahmaputra but it flows through Sikkim.
2. River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a tributary of river Teesta.
3. River Teesta flows into Bay of Bengal on the border of India and Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Teesta rises in Sikkim, not at the Brahmaputra's source, and joins the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh rather than the sea. The Rangeet rises in Sikkim and is its tributary.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In tropical regions, Zika virus disease is transmitted by the same mosquito that transmits dengue.
2. Sexual transmission of Zika virus disease is possible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Zika is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, the same ones that carry dengue, and it can also be transmitted sexually. Both statements are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Standard Mark of Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes.
2. AGMARK is a quality Certification Mark issued by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The BIS mark is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes. AGMARK is an Indian mark issued by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, not the FAO.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q32

questions.q:
What is/are the advantage/advantages of implementing the ‘National Agriculture Market’ scheme?
1. It is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities.
2. It provides the farmers access to nationwide market, with prices commensurate with the quality of their produce.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: e-NAM is a pan-India online trading platform linking mandis, giving farmers a nationwide market and quality-based prices. Both statements are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘National Intellectual Property Rights Policy’, consider the following statements:
1. It reiterates India’s commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and the TRIPS Agreement.
2. Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion is the nodal agency for regulating intellectual property rights in India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: The National IPR Policy (2016) reaffirms India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and TRIPS, and makes DIPP the nodal agency for IPRs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q:
According to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which of the following animals cannot be hunted by any person except under some provisions provided by law?
1. Gharial
2. Indian wild ass
3. Wild buffalo
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Gharial, Indian wild ass and wild buffalo are all in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, so they cannot be hunted except as the Act permits.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen?
1. A legislative process has been provided to enforce these duties.
2. They are correlative to legal duties.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Constitution provides no machinery to enforce the Fundamental Duties, and they are not tied to legal duties. Neither statement is true.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Radhakanta Deb — First President of the British Indian Association
2. Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty — Founder of the Madras Mahajana Sabha
3. Surendranath Banerjee — Founder of the Indian Association
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Radhakanta Deb was the first president of the British Indian Association (1851) and Surendranath Banerjee founded the Indian Association (1876). Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association, not the Mahajana Sabha.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q: Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
questions.e: The Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship. 'Economic' appears only with justice, not liberty.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Quality Council of India (QCI)’, consider the following statements:
1. QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian Industry.
2. Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendations of the industry to the Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: QCI was set up jointly by the Government and Indian industry, and its Chairman is appointed by the Prime Minister on industry's recommendation. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q:
What is the purpose of setting up of Small Finance Banks (SFBs) in India?
1. To supply credit to small business units
2. To supply credit to small and marginal farmers
3. To encourage young entrepreneurs to set up business particularly in rural areas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Small Finance Banks were created for financial inclusion: to offer savings and supply credit to small businesses, small and marginal farmers and the unorganised sector. Encouraging young rural entrepreneurs is not a stated aim.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q40

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Asia Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development (APMCHUD)’, consider the following statements:
1. The first APMCHUD was held in India in 2006 on the theme ‘Emerging Urban Forms — Policy Responses and Governance Structure’.
2. India hosts all the Annual Ministerial Conferences in partnership with ADB, APEC and ASEAN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The first APMCHUD was held in New Delhi in 2006, but on a different theme. It is biennial and hosted by different countries, so neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q: Democracy’s superior virtue lies in the fact that it calls into activity
o: the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women.
the methods for strengthening executive leadership.
a superior individual with dynamism and vision.
a band of dedicated party workers.
questions.e: Democracy's special strength is that it involves ordinary citizens and draws on their judgement and character.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q: Which of the following is a most likely consequence of implementing the ‘Unified Payments Interface (UPI)’?
o: Mobile wallets will not be necessary for online payments.
Digital currency will totally replace the physical currency in about two decades.
Direct transfer of subsidies to poor people will become very effective.
questions.e: UPI transfers money directly between bank accounts through one app, so there is no need to load money into a mobile wallet first.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q: The terms ‘Event Horizon’, ‘Singularity’, ‘String Theory’ and ‘Standard Model’ are sometimes seen in the news in the context of
o: Observation and understanding of the Universe
Study of the solar and the lunar eclipses
Placing satellites in the orbit of the Earth
Origin and evolution of living organisms on the Earth
questions.e: Event horizon and singularity relate to black holes; string theory and the Standard Model explain matter and forces. All concern understanding the Universe.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q44

questions.q:
With reference to agriculture in India, how can the technique of ‘genome sequencing’, often seen in the news, be used in the immediate future?
1. Genome sequencing can be used to identify genetic markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance in various crop plants.
2. This technique helps in reducing the time required to develop new varieties of crop plants.
3. It can be used to decipher the host-pathogen relationships in crops.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Genome sequencing finds markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance, speeds up breeding of new varieties, and reveals host-pathogen interactions. All three are uses.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that
o: the executive and legislature work independently.
it provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
the executive remains responsible to the legislature.
the head of the government cannot be changed without election.
questions.e: The defining feature of parliamentary government is that the executive is collectively responsible to the legislature (Article 75(3)).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties?
o: Rights are personal and hence independent of society and Duties.
Rights, not Duties, are important for the advancement of the personality of the citizen.
Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State.
questions.e: Rights and duties go together: each right brings a duty to respect the same right of others.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following?
o: The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble sums up the philosophy and objectives of the Constitution's makers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q: If you travel by road from Kohima to Kottayam, what is the minimum number of States within India through which you can travel, including the origin and the destination?
questions.e: The shortest chain of bordering states is Nagaland, Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala: seven states.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q:
The Parliament of India exercises control over the functions of the Council of Ministers through
1. Adjournment motion
2. Question hour
3. Supplementary questions
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Adjournment motions, question hour and supplementary questions are all ways Parliament holds ministers accountable.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
questions.e: Motupalli on the Andhra coast was the main Kakatiya port; Ganapatideva issued an edict there guaranteeing safety to foreign merchants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Global Climate Change Alliance’, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is an initiative of the European Union.
2. It provides technical and financial support to targeted developing countries to integrate climate change into their development policies and budgets.
3. It is coordinated by World Resources Institute (WRI) and World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD).
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Global Climate Change Alliance is an EU initiative (2007) that helps vulnerable developing countries build climate change into their policies and budgets. It is not run by WRI and WBCSD.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q:
With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements:
1. Sautrantika and Sammitiya were the sects of Jainism.
2. Sarvastivadin held that the constituents of phenomena were not wholly momentary, but existed forever in a latent form.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Sautrantika and Sammitiya were Buddhist schools, not Jain. Sarvastivadins held that the elements of existence persist in a latent form, so 2 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
Mediterranean Sea is a border of which of the following countries?
1. Jordan
2. Iraq
3. Lebanon
4. Syria
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Of these, only Lebanon and Syria have a Mediterranean coast. Jordan touches only the Gulf of Aqaba and Iraq the Persian Gulf.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q:
With reference to ‘National Investment and Infrastructure Fund’, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is an organ of NITI Aayog.
2. It has a corpus of ₹ 4,00,000 crore at present.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: NIIF (2015) is a Finance Ministry-backed investment fund, not part of NITI Aayog, and its planned corpus was ₹40,000 crore. Neither statement holds.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q: The Global Infrastructure Facility is a/an
o: ASEAN initiative to upgrade infrastructure in Asia and financed by credit from the Asian Development Bank.

World Bank collaboration that facilitates the preparation and structuring of complex infrastructure Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) to enable mobilization of private sector and institutional investor capital.
Collaboration among the major banks of the world working with the OECD and focused on expanding the set of infrastructure projects that have the potential to mobilize private investment.
UNCTAD funded initiative that seeks to finance and facilitate infrastructure development in the world.
questions.e: The Global Infrastructure Facility, a G20 initiative hosted by the World Bank, helps prepare and structure complex infrastructure PPPs to attract private capital.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q: For election to the Lok Sabha, a nomination paper can be filed by
o: a resident of the constituency from which the election is to be contested.
any citizen of India whose name appears in the electoral roll of a constituency.
questions.e: A Lok Sabha candidate must be an Indian citizen registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency, not necessarily the one contested.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, the Himalayas are spread over five States only.
2. Western Ghats are spread over five States only.
3. Pulicat Lake is spread over two States only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Pulicat Lake lies in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu only. The Himalayas cover far more than five states and the Western Ghats run through six.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard criterion for
o: Computing oxygen levels in forest ecosystems
Assessing oxygen levels in high altitude regions
questions.e: BOD is the oxygen microbes need to break down organic matter in water; a high BOD means more organic pollution.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q:
With reference to the role of UN-Habitat in the United Nations programme working towards a better urban future, which of the statements is/are correct?
1. UN-Habitat has been mandated by the United Nations General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities to provide adequate shelter for all.
2. Its partners are either governments or local urban authorities only.
3. UN-Habitat contributes to the overall objective of the United Nations system to reduce poverty and to promote access to safe drinking water and basic sanitation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: UN-Habitat promotes sustainable towns and cities and works on poverty, water and sanitation. Its partners include NGOs, academia and the private sector, not just governments.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q:
With reference to ‘National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF)’, which of the statements given below is/are correct?
1. Under NSQF, a learner can acquire the certification for competency only through formal learning.
2. An outcome expected from the implementation of NSQF is the mobility between vocational and general education.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: NSQF certifies competencies however they were learnt, including informally, so 1 is wrong. It aims to allow movement between vocational and general education.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q: In the context of Indian history, the principle of ‘Dyarchy (diarchy)’ refers to
o: Division of the central legislature into two houses.
Introduction of double government i.e., Central and State governments.
Having two sets of rulers; one in London and another in Delhi.
Division of the subjects delegated to the provinces into two categories.
questions.e: Dyarchy under the 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into 'reserved' (Governor and council) and 'transferred' (Indian ministers responsible to the legislature).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q:
Consider the following in respect of ‘National Career Service’:
1. National Career Service is an initiative of the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India.
2. National Career Service has been launched in a Mission Mode to improve the employment opportunities to uneducated youth of the country.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: The National Career Service is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment and serves all job seekers. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes the term ‘Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A)’, recently seen in the news?
o: It is a procedure for considering ecological costs of developmental schemes formulated by the Government.
It is a scheme of RBI for reworking the financial structure of big corporate entities facing genuine difficulties.
It is a disinvestment plan of the Government regarding Central Public Sector Undertakings.
It is an important provision in ‘The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code’ recently implemented by the Government.
questions.e: S4A was an RBI scheme letting banks rework the debt structure of large companies in genuine difficulty.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) to Reduce Short Lived Climate Pollutants is a unique initiative of G20 group of countries.
2. The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon and hydrofluorocarbons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is a voluntary partnership convened by UNEP, not a G20 initiative. It targets methane, black carbon and HFCs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q:
With reference to ‘Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)’ sometimes mentioned in the news while forecasting Indian monsoon, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. IOD phenomenon is characterised by a difference in sea surface temperature between tropical Western Indian Ocean and tropical Eastern Pacific Ocean.
2. An IOD phenomenon can influence an El Nino’s impact on the monsoon.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The IOD is the temperature difference between the western and south-eastern tropical Indian Ocean, not the Pacific. A positive IOD can offset El Nino's effect on the monsoon.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q: If you want to see gharials in their natural habitat, which one of the following is the best place to visit?
questions.e: The National Chambal Sanctuary holds the world's largest wild gharial population.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q:
Consider the following in respect of Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS):
1. Inaugural IONS was held in India in 2015 under the chairmanship of the Indian Navy.
2. IONS is a voluntary initiative that seeks to increase maritime co-operation among navies of the littoral states of the Indian Ocean Region.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: The first IONS was held in New Delhi in 2008, not 2015. It is a voluntary forum for maritime co-operation among Indian Ocean navies.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani is one of the most famous and oft-illustrated paintings at
questions.e: The Bodhisattva Padmapani painting is in Cave 1 at Ajanta.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Traditions Communities
1. Chaliha Sahib Festival Sindhis
2. Nanda Raj Jaat Yatra Gonds
3. Wari-Warkari Santhals
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Chaliha Sahib is a Sindhi festival. Nanda Raj Jaat is a Himalayan pilgrimage in Uttarakhand and Wari is a Maharashtra pilgrimage, so only 1 is right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q:
Which of the following practices can help in water conservation in agriculture?
1. Reduced or zero tillage of the land
2. Applying gypsum before irrigating the field
3. Allowing crop residue to remain in the field
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Zero tillage and leaving crop residue cut evaporation and help water soak in. Gypsum treats sodic soils; it does not save water.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: The nation-wide ‘Soil Health Card Scheme’ aims at
1. expanding the cultivable area under irrigation.
2. enabling the banks to assess the quantum of loans to be granted to farmers on the basis of soil quality.
3. checking the overuse of fertilizers in farmlands.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: Soil Health Cards tell farmers the nutrient status of their soil and the fertiliser doses to use, curbing overuse. They are not for irrigation or bank lending.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Commonly used / consumed materials Unwanted or controversial chemicals likely to be found in them
1. Lipstick Lead
2. Soft drinks Brominated vegetable oils
3. Chinese fast food Monosodium glutamate
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Lead in lipstick, brominated vegetable oil in soft drinks and MSG in Chinese fast food have all raised health concerns. All three pairs are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q:
Organic Light Emitting Diodes (OLEDs) are used to create digital display in many devices. What are the advantages of OLED displays over Liquid Crystal displays?
1. OLED displays can be fabricated on flexible plastic substrates.
2. Roll-up displays embedded in clothing can be made using OLEDs.
3. Transparent displays are possible using OLEDs.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: None of the above statements is correct
questions.e: OLED pixels make their own light and need no backlight, so displays can be flexible, rollable and transparent. All three are advantages.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are famous for Sun temples?
1. Arasavalli
2. Amarakantak
3. Omkareshwar
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Arasavalli in Andhra Pradesh has a famous Sun temple. Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and Omkareshwar has a Shiva Jyotirlinga.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the election for Lok Sabha or State Assembly, the winning candidate must get at least 50 percent of the votes polled, to be declared elected.
2. According to the provisions laid down in the Constitution of India, in Lok Sabha, the Speaker’s post goes to the majority party and the Deputy Speaker’s to the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Elections are won by the most votes (first past the post), not 50%. The Constitution does not reserve the Speaker or Deputy Speaker post for any party.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q:
Which of the following has/have occurred in India after its liberalization of economic policies in 1991?
1. Share of agriculture in GDP increased enormously.
2. Share of India’s exports in world trade increased.
3. FDI inflows increased.
4. India’s foreign exchange reserves increased enormously.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: After 1991 India's export share, FDI inflows and forex reserves rose, while agriculture's share of GDP fell.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q: What is the application of Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer Technology?
o: Production of organisms free of diseases
questions.e: Somatic cell nuclear transfer puts the nucleus of a body cell into an enucleated egg; it is the technique for cloning animals, as with Dolly.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) helps in promoting the financial inclusion in the country.
2. NPCI has launched RuPay, a card payment scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NPCI runs India's retail payment systems and promotes financial inclusion; RuPay is its domestic card scheme. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q: The term ‘M-STrIPES’ is sometimes seen in the news in the context of
questions.e: M-STrIPES is the NTCA's monitoring system for tigers, used for patrolling and ecological monitoring in tiger reserves.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q:
What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing ‘Goods and Services Tax (GST)’?
1. It will replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities and will thus create a single market in India.
2. It will drastically reduce the ‘Current Account Deficit’ of India and will enable it to increase its foreign exchange reserves.
3. It will enormously increase the growth and size of economy of India and will enable it to overtake China in the near future.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: GST replaced many central and state taxes, creating a single national market. Claims about cutting the current account deficit or overtaking China are exaggerated.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q: ‘Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement (BTIA)’ is sometimes seen in the news in the context of negotiations held between India and
o: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.e: BTIA is the India-EU free trade agreement under negotiation since 2007.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India has ratified the Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) of WTO.
2. TFA is a part of WTO’s Bali Ministerial Package of 2013.
3. TFA came into force in January 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India ratified the WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement in 2016, and the TFA was part of the 2013 Bali package. It entered into force in February 2017, not January 2016.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q83

questions.q: What is the importance of developing Chabahar Port by India?
o: India’s trade with African countries will enormously increase.
India’s relations with oil-producing Arab countries will be strengthened.
India will not depend on Pakistan for access to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
Pakistan will facilitate and protect the installation of a gas pipeline between Iraq and India.
questions.e: Chabahar port in Iran gives India a route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q:
In India, it is legally mandatory for which of the following to report on cyber security incidents?
1. Service providers
2. Data centres
3. Body corporate
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Under the IT Act and CERT-In rules, service providers, data centres and body corporates must report cyber incidents.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q: Right to vote and to be elected in India is a
questions.e: The right to vote comes from Article 326 (adult suffrage), so it is a constitutional right, but not a Fundamental Right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q: What is the purpose of ‘evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (eLISA)’ project?
o: To detect the effectiveness of missile defence system
To study the effect of solar flares on our communication systems
questions.e: eLISA was a planned space-based laser interferometer to detect gravitational waves.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q:
What is the purpose of ‘Vidyanjali Yojana’?
1. To enable the famous foreign educational institutions to open their campuses in India.
2. To increase the quality of education provided in government schools by taking help from the private sector and the community.
3. To encourage voluntary monetary contributions from private individuals and organizations so as to improve the infrastructure facilities for primary and secondary schools.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Vidyanjali brings volunteers from the community and private sector into government schools to improve learning. It is not about foreign campuses or cash donations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q: What is the aim of the programme ‘Unnat Bharat Abhiyan’?
o: Achieving 100% literacy by promoting collaboration between voluntary organizations and government’s education system and local communities.
Connecting institutions of higher education with local communities to address development challenges through appropriate technologies.
Strengthening India’s scientific research institutions in order to make India a scientific and technological power.
Developing human capital by allocating special funds for health care and education of rural and urban poor, and organizing skill development programmes and vocational training for them.
questions.e: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan links higher education institutions with villages to solve local development problems with suitable technologies.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Election Commission of India is a five-member body.
2. Union Ministry of Home Affairs decides the election schedule for the conduct of both general elections and bye-elections.
3. Election Commission resolves the disputes relating to splits/mergers of recognised political parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Election Commission (CEC plus two commissioners) sets election schedules itself and settles disputes over party splits and mergers under the Symbols Order. Only 3 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q: In India, if a species of tortoise is declared protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, what does it imply?
o: It enjoys the same level of protection as the tiger.
It no longer exists in the wild, a few individuals are under captive protection; and now it is impossible to prevent its extinction.
It is endemic to a particular region of India.
Both (b) and (c) stated above are correct in this context.
questions.e: Schedule I gives the highest protection, the same as the tiger. It says nothing about extinction in the wild or endemism.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q91

questions.q: In India, Judicial Review implies
o: the power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
the power of the Judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the Legislatures.
the power of the Judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President.
the power of the Judiciary to review its own judgements given earlier in similar or different cases.
questions.e: Judicial review is the courts' power to test laws and executive orders against the Constitution and strike down those that violate it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q92
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
With reference to Indian freedom struggle, consider the following events:
1. Mutiny in Royal Indian Navy
2. Quit India Movement launched
3. Second Round Table Conference
What is the correct chronological sequence of the above events?
questions.e: Second Round Table Conference: 1931; Quit India: August 1942; Royal Indian Navy mutiny: February 1946. So 3-2-1.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tax revenue as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
2. Fiscal deficit as a percent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither ratio rose steadily: tax-to-GDP hovered around 10% and the fiscal deficit spiked in 2009-10 and then fell.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q: Recently there was a proposal to translocate some of the lions from their natural habitat in Gujarat to which one of the following sites?
questions.e: Kuno-Palpur in Madhya Pradesh was chosen as a second home for Asiatic lions, so that one disaster in Gujarat could not wipe them out.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q:
Which of the following are not necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President’s rule in a State?
1. Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly
2. Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State
3. Dissolution of the local bodies
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Under President's rule the State Council of Ministers is always dismissed, but the Assembly may be only suspended and local bodies are untouched. So 1 and 3 are not necessary.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India?
1. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
2. Abolition of untouchability
3. Protection of the interests of minorities
4. Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Right against Exploitation is Articles 23 (trafficking, forced labour) and 24 (child labour in factories and mines). Untouchability and minorities fall under other rights.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q: Which of the following is geographically closest to Great Nicobar?
questions.e: Indira Point on Great Nicobar is only about 150 km from Sumatra; Java, Borneo and Sri Lanka are much farther.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government:
o: An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.
questions.e: The core principle of Cabinet government is collective responsibility of the ministry to the elected House, and through it to the people.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Indian federalism?
o: There is an independent judiciary in India.
Powers have been clearly divided between the Centre and the States.
The federating units have been given unequal representation in the Rajya Sabha.
It is the result of an agreement among the federating units.
questions.e: India's federation was not formed by an agreement among states; it is a 'Union of States' that cannot be broken up by them.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2017, GS Paper I, Q100
